A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey and support comparison of the complete text, figures, tables and references. Neither contains an appendix. Minor visible text defects in v11 do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v10 synthesizes cited research and provides conceptual illustrations. Its tables catalogue existing work, and Figure 27's example scores are illustrative; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v11 remains a literature survey. Added performance statements about UFO2, ViMo and other systems are attributed to cited works, rather than experiments or data analyses conducted for this survey.

M1.justification: The generic perception, prompting, inference, action and memory workflow remains unchanged. Added descriptions concern cited systems; they do not establish a revision to an algorithm proposed by this work.

E1.justification: New entries such as InSTA and LearnGUI expand the literature catalogue. Neither version actually trains or evaluates its own system on these datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version conducts an experimental comparison against a proposed method. Added accounts of UFO2, Agent S2 and other systems therefore do not constitute changes to an evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: The survey does not implement an evaluation protocol in either version. Added benchmark descriptions and the new Live classification document external evaluation resources, rather than change experiments performed by this work.

E4.justification: Existing illustrative examples of memory, reflection, evaluation and human interaction are retained. The new UFO2 illustrations explain a cited system; no original ablation, robustness test or empirical case analysis is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests for original results. The new account of Computer Agent Arena's Elo ranking describes an external benchmark, not a statistical analysis performed by the survey.

E6.justification: v11 adds cited performance findings: UFO2 reportedly exceeds Operator and other CUAs by over 10 percentage points while halving LLM calls (Section 6.3), and ViMo reports a 29.14% relative improvement in GUI generation metrics (Section 8.4). These are newly summarized literature results, not same-setting performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: The conceptual definitions and MDP framing are retained. Additional system descriptions and categorical tables introduce no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, survey scope and research questions in Section 1.2, and conclusion are unchanged. The central contributions remain a comprehensive survey, construction guide and research roadmap.

C2.justification: Section 11 retains its seven challenge areas but adds more specific discussion of data scoping, cross-application error propagation, shared control, traceability and virtual-desktop isolation. Section 8.7 adds an interpretation of inference-time reasoning as an emerging direction.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 adds guidance on system-prompt placement and dynamic supplementary instructions. New resource entries provide technical descriptions, model sizes, collection pipelines and access links, including for UFO2 and InSTA. The survey's own repository and searchable webpage remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v11 retains all 563 earlier references and adds 62, substantially extending coverage of reasoning and reinforcement learning, skill acquisition, AgentOS systems, datasets, benchmarks and security. Section 2 also expands comparisons with other surveys and clarifies the work's lifecycle-wide positioning.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in related-work positioning, platform exposition and Section 11's challenge discussions; the overall twelve-section organization remains intact. v11 also introduces visible word corruption in Section 9, including missing letters in 'autonomously'.

P2.justification: v11 adds the platform comparison in Table 3 and UFO2 illustrations in Figures 24 and 32. Multiple catalogues are expanded and split, and benchmark tables gain a Live column. Existing illustrations are retained and relocated. Table 37 incorrectly places 'AutoEval' in its Live cell.

improvement.justification: The new platform comparison, expanded coverage of emerging techniques and more specific deployment limitations improve the survey's practical guidance. These incremental benefits outweigh the localized deterioration from damaged words in Section 9 and the erroneous AutoEval Live entry in Table 37; the core survey contribution remains stable.
